title: Northern Yan
capsule: Northern Yan was one of the Sixteen Kingdoms of China, a dynastic state ruling the northeastern region of Liaodong and part of Hebei from 410 to 436 CE. It originated when Feng Ba, an official of the Later Yan, overthrew his Murong Xianbei ruler and proclaimed a new state, breaking the Xianbei monopoly on northern Chinese kingship. Feng Ba (r. 409–430) and his brother Feng Hong (r. 430–436) patronized Chinese literary culture and maintained a functioning court; when Northern Wei attacked, Feng Hong fled in 436 with his court to the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo, where he was eventually killed in 438, ending the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Northern Yan's territory is reasonably attested through Chinese dynastic histories (Jin Shu, Wei Shu); its boundaries with Northern Wei and Goguryeo are approximately known but the exact frontier lines are uncertain.
